ui.canvas_label: {{$beat_title}}: the light at {{$l_travelled}} kpc along the beam

B0.sub: Ride one beam of quasar light through the gas around galaxy 488530.
B0.sub_short: Ride one beam of quasar light.

B1.display: This light left a quasar long ago.
B1.sub: The strip below is this quasar's light, as a perfect telescope riding with it would record it. For now, all of it gets through.
B1.sub_short: For now, all the light gets through.

B2.display: Galaxies sit inside gas *too faint to see.*
B2.sub: The gas shows itself only by the light it takes from things behind it. These colours are our choice, not its light.
B2.sub_short: It shows only by the light it takes.

B2.1.display: We ride this one beam through it.
B2.1.sub: Every beam meets different gas, so every spectrum differs. Pick another beam at any time.

B3.display: Every cell has a density, heat and speed.
B3.sub: The beam touches hundreds of gas cells. Each one lights up as the light reaches it.
B3.sub_short: Each cell lights up as the light arrives.

B3.1.display: So far, almost nothing is taken.
B3.1.sub: By now O VI has taken 1.1 % of the light at its deepest colour.
B3.1.sub_short: O VI has taken 1.1 % so far.

B4.sub: Atoms take a sliver of one colour out of the light: the first cell's dip was 5.6 % deep. The rest goes on.
B4.sub_short: Atoms take a sliver of one colour.

B5.1.display: *One hydrogen atom in ten keeps its electron.*
B5.1.sub: That is at its core. In warm-hot gas only one in 200 000 does: about 20 000 times fewer. Neutral hydrogen takes the colour we follow.
B5.1.sub_short: Neutral hydrogen takes the colour we follow.

B5.2.display: One clump, and the dip is black.
B5.2.sub: Hydrogen's dip goes black within a few cells. Its warm-hot skin comes next: O VI loses another 32 % of its light.

B6.display: Here the gas is *too hot to see.*
B6.sub: So hot that oxygen loses even a sixth electron and hydrogen keeps almost none. O VI and H I take almost no light here.
B6.sub_short: Too hot for much O VI or H I.

B6.1.sub: Moving toward us shifts a shadow bluer, like a siren. Cloud A's dip sits left for its speed, not its order.
B6.1.sub_short: Toward us shifts bluer, like a siren.

B7b.display: Amount sets how much light is taken.
B7b.sub: This one cell holds a quarter of all the O VI on the beam. Its dip grows term by term: amount, width, place.
B7b.sub_short: One cell holds a quarter of the O VI.

B7b.1.sub: Hotter ions jiggle faster, so the same amount spreads over more speeds: wider and shallower.

B7c.display: Change the heat, watch the dip.
B7c.sub: Warmer gas spreads the dip wider. But O VI lives only in a band of heat: outside it, the dip fades.
B7c.sub_short: O VI lives in a band of heat.

B7c.hot.display: Too hot: oxygen loses another electron.
B7c.hot.sub: Above 3.9×10⁵ K the O VI share here falls below half its peak, and the dip fades.

B7c.cool.display: Too cool: oxygen keeps more electrons.
B7c.cool.sub: Below 2.4×10⁵ K the O VI share here falls below half its peak, and the dip fades.

B7d.display: One cloud, many speeds, a wide dip.
B7d.sub: Each cell adds its own shadow at its own speed. The shadows stack: each passes a share of the light left.
B7d.sub_short: Shadows stack; each passes a share of what is left.

B7e.sub: A second cool cloud hides in the black H I dip: about +37 km/s at its densest. O VI beside it: −55 and +14 km/s.
B7e.sub_short: A second cool cloud, hidden in black.

B8.display: Halfway. The galaxy sits beside us.
B8.sub: Its centre is 202 000 light-years to the side. Closest does not mean most gas: 69.5 % of the O VI is already behind us.
B8.sub_short: Its centre: 202 000 light-years to the side.

B9.sub: New O VI dips appear at +61, +98 km/s. The order of dips is not the order of clouds.
B9.sub_short: Dip order is not cloud order.

B9.1.sub: Gas 84 kpc apart moves at almost the same speed, so the spectrum cannot tell them apart: the clearest of 2 such pairs.

B9.2.display: The spectrum keeps speed and loses place.
B9.2.sub: A dip records how fast gas moves along the beam, not where it sits.

B10.sub: More atoms darken a dip's centre while its width hardly changes, until the centre is black.

B10.1.sub: Cloud D's hydrogen lands on a dip that is already black: the trough widens, but cannot get darker.

B11.display: This is everything *the light carried out.*
B11.sub: 49 cells left a visible O VI shadow. Their shadows merged into a few broad dips.

B12a.sub: Every telescope smears the spectrum a little. Less sharpness means neighbouring dips blend into one.

B12a.1.sub: A narrow black dip comes out grey, as if light got through. The wide hydrogen trough stays black.

B12b.sub: Twice as clean needs four times as long. The noise pattern stays the same; only its size shrinks.
B12b.sub_short: Twice as clean takes four times longer.

B12b.1.display: Noise can hide dips, *and invent them.*
B12b.1.sub: At low exposure the smaller dip at +96 km/s drowns, and chance wiggles look like dips. The white line is the truth.
B12b.1.sub_short: The white line is the truth.

B13.sub: A fit explains the noisy spectrum with a few smooth components, each with an amount, a width and a speed.
B13.sub_short: Each has an amount, width and speed.

B13.1.sub: One component can draw on gas in several places, and clouds are not cells: one clump, many cells across, can feed several components.
B13.1.sub_short: Many to many. Clouds are not cells.

B13.3.display: A spectrum tells how much and how fast.
B13.3.sub: …but not where, and one width alone is not a thermometer.
B13.3.sub_short: Not where. One width is no thermometer.

B14.display: Now it is yours. Same galaxy, same beam.
B14.sub: Change sharpness and exposure, pick another of 198 galaxies, or open this beam in the explorer.

B14.1.sub: This beam has no cell-by-cell ride yet: you see its library spectrum, and the cells drawn did not make it.
B14.1.sub_short: Library spectrum; drawn cells are not its cells.

B7d.sub_short: Shadows stack; each passes a share of what is left.

B7e.sub: A second cool cloud hides in the black H I dip: about +37 km/s at its densest. O VI beside it: −55 and +14 km/s.
B7e.sub_short: A second cool cloud, hidden in black.

B8.display: Halfway. The galaxy sits beside us.
B8.sub: Its centre is 202 000 light-years to the side. Closest does not mean most gas: 69.5 % of the O VI is already behind us.
B8.sub_short: Its centre: 202 000 light-years to the side.

B9.sub: New O VI dips appear at +61, +98 km/s. The order of dips is not the order of clouds.
B9.sub_short: Dip order is not cloud order.

B9.1.sub: Gas 84 kpc apart moves at almost the same speed, so the spectrum cannot tell them apart: the clearest of 2 such pairs.

B9.2.display: The spectrum keeps speed and loses place.
B9.2.sub: A dip records how fast gas moves along the beam, not where it sits.

B10.sub: More atoms darken a dip's centre while its width hardly changes, until the centre is black.

B10.1.sub: Cloud D's hydrogen lands on a dip that is already black: the trough widens, but cannot get darker.

B11.display: This is everything *the light carried out.*

B12a.sub: Every telescope smears the spectrum a little. Less sharpness means neighbouring dips blend into one.

B12a.1.sub: A narrow black dip comes out grey, as if light got through. The wide hydrogen trough stays black.

B12b.sub_short: Twice as clean takes four times longer.

B12b.1.sub_short: The white line is the truth.

B13.3.sub_short: Not where. One width is no thermometer.
